title: Ledger security bulletins LSB 023-025
notes: Bounded security-event update for existing Ledger entity wlr_ent_000002. The Ledger Ethereum device application and Ledger Secure SDK are not modeled as standalone WLR products, so affected_product_ids remain empty rather than attributing the findings to specific hardware models without product-level evidence.

events.title: Ledger disclosed command-interleaving signing vulnerability class
events.description: Ledger disclosed that applications built with affected Ledger Secure SDK releases could accept a new APDU command while an earlier command was awaiting on-screen user review, allowing signing parameters held in application state to be changed after display but before signature generation when an application did not independently validate its state machine.
affected_versions: Ledger Secure SDK releases from the August 2025 regression through v26.6.0; exposure depends on application-level state validation
events.notes: LSB 023 states that the defect was in Ledger Secure SDK input/output event handling rather than device OS/firmware. Ethereum app 1.22.2, published 2026-08-13, was the first application release carrying application-level state guards. Ledger Secure SDK v26.6.1, released 2026-08-21, removed the interleaving opportunity generically and applications were rebuilt against it. Ledger reports no evidence of exploitation. Users must update device applications through Ledger Live; firmware update alone does not establish remediation.

events.title: Ledger disclosed Ethereum clear-signing array-count truncation vulnerability
events.description: Ledger disclosed an Ethereum app Generic Transaction Parser flaw in which an attacker-controlled 16-bit array element count was stored in an 8-bit countdown field. For a 257-element array, the device could review only one operation while its signature still authorized the complete transaction.
events.notes: LSB 024 records Ledger's High classification of the reported flaw. Exploitation requires a compromised host plus a clear-signing descriptor iterating an attacker-controlled array of more than 255 elements. Ledger reports no production frontend compromise, public-network proof of concept, real-fund movement, or known exploitation. Ethereum app 1.22.3, published 2026-08-25, contains the correction; users should install 1.22.3 or later.

events.title: Ledger disclosed Ethereum swap token-approval substitution vulnerability
events.description: Ledger disclosed an Ethereum app flaw in the token-payment path used by the Exchange application during swaps: the path checked the expected address and quantity but not the requested operation type, so a token approval carrying the expected values could pass validation and be signed without being displayed as an approval.
events.notes: LSB 025 states that the approval itself does not transfer funds but grants spending permission that can be used by a later transaction. Ledger reports no evidence of exploitation. Ethereum app 1.22.3, published 2026-08-25, corrects the operation-type validation; users should install 1.22.3 or later and verify the application version on the signer. Firmware update alone does not establish that the affected application has been replaced.

evidence.title: Ledger Security Bulletin 023 — Command interleaving during an on-screen review could desynchronise the display from the signature
evidence.notes: Primary Ledger security bulletin supporting the vulnerability class, affected SDK boundary, Ethereum app 1.22.2 application-level hardening, Secure SDK v26.6.1 generic correction, lack of known exploitation, and application-update remediation boundary.

evidence.title: Ledger Security Bulletin 024 — Clear-signing bypass via array-count truncation in the Ethereum app
evidence.notes: Primary Ledger security bulletin supporting the 1.19.0-1.22.2 affected range, High classification, exploit preconditions, no-real-funds/no-known-exploitation boundary, and Ethereum app 1.22.3 correction.

evidence.title: Ledger Security Bulletin 025 — Swap flow accepted a token approval in place of a payment
evidence.notes: Primary Ledger security bulletin supporting the 1.20.0-1.22.2 affected range, token-approval substitution mechanism, lack of known exploitation, and Ethereum app 1.22.3 correction.
